1.why: /api/reset-validate and /api/password-update require token === session.resetToken, and that token is only stored server-side when the request email matches the known mock account, binding the code to that user's session.

2.why: The reset token is stored per session and only for the mock account, so a code issued in one session fails validation in any other session (token === session.resetToken).

3.why: Password update only flags the current session (session.resetUsed = true) and nothing revokes other sessions, which remain usable until the 30-minute TTL sweeper removes them.

4.why: The app serves only over TLS with HSTS, rejects plain HTTP (426) and non-HTTPS requests (421), but the TLS version is not explicitly pinned, so 'latest' relies on runtime defaults.

5.why: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt (cost 12) and tokens are 32-byte CSPRNG values, though the reset token itself is held in plaintext in the in-memory session rather than hashed or encrypted.

6.why: No real email is sent; the simulated local delivery message contains only the reset code plus never-share guidance, with no other private user data exposed.

7.why: Email is trimmed/lowercased and regex-validated, passwords are policy-validated, JSON bodies are size-capped and type-checked, and all UI rendering uses textContent/createElement with no HTML injection.

8.why: There are no HTTP redirects or user-controlled links anywhere; navigation is internal screens only, Origin is allowlisted, and CSP sets form-action 'self'.

9.why: There are no email templates; the simulated delivery strings are fixed literals rendered via textContent, and a nonce-based CSP blocks any inline or injected script.

10.why: All error responses are generic messages and the catch-all 500 hides stack traces, but the in-page 'Logs' panel intentionally displays the reset and MFA codes as the simulated delivery channel.

11.why: Passwords are never in the code, but the MFA verification code ("482913") and the mock account email are hardcoded constants in the source.

12.why: There is no login endpoint and no default username/password exists, though the single static MFA code effectively acts as a shared second factor for every recovery.

13.why: rateAllowed throttles reset requests (3/15 min), code guesses (5/15 min), and MFA attempts (5/15 min), but counters are keyed to the session cookie so a fresh session resets the limits.

14.why: /api/reset-request returns the identical generic message and an opaque token for any valid-format email regardless of whether the account exists.

15.why: Reset codes are 256-bit CSPRNG base64url tokens, single-use, with 15-minute expiry, and are stored only for the mock account's session.
